messages:
sasha: Quick update on onboarding phoenix-27b-x (fp16 -> int8-lite).
sasha: Bench shows ~1.8x token/s improvement, memory footprint down ~30%, but two issues:
sasha: 1) ~6% drop on our commonsense QA EM metric in the nightly eval. 2) intermittent OOMs under bursty microbatching (seen on gpu-3).
priya: Can you paste the OOM snippet and the exact command you used? :eyes:
sasha: Sure — minimal excerpt from node logs:
```
OOM at alloc 245M after kv-cache grow
stack: alloc -> kv-cache -> attention-kernel
node: gpu-3
cmd: /bin/redwood-run --model phoenix-27b-x --quant int8-lite --batch 3 --max_new_tokens 256 --prefetch on
```
dmitri: Two immediate mitigations to try:
- tighten defaults: batch_size 2, max_new_tokens 128
- enable a soft GPU reserve so allocs fail earlier and we fallback instead of hard OOM
Suggested config snippet for model defaults:
```
model_defaults:
  batch_size: 2
  max_new_tokens: 128
  soft_mem_reserve_mb: 600
  prefetch: false
```
ciara: About the 6% EM drop — what's the eval scope and sample size? If it's a small holdout the delta could be noisy.
sasha: Eval details: run on 5k QA pairs (mixed open-domain + commonsense). Baseline fp16: EM 72.4, int8-lite: EM 66.9. Hallucination rate up ~2.1% absolute. Metrics and examples attached to the PR.
kevin: Hypothesis: quant noise in logits for low-confidence spans + batching-induced softmax scaling differences. Ops to consider:
- staged quant rollout (phasewise): bench-only -> tiny canary -> A/B with quality monitor
- fallback to fp16 for routes hitting quality thresholds
Also propose a routing + fallback policy to reduce blast radius.
sasha: Proposed rollout plan (conservative):
1) Overnight synthetic bench across 6 instance types (measure p99/p50 and mem). 2) Canary: 0.5% traffic, enforced batch cap=1, max_new_tokens default=96, prefetch off. 3) If no OOMs and EM drop <2% relative, step to 2% traffic and batch cap=2 for 24h. 4) Full switch with gradual batch increase and telemetry gating.
Command-ish routing example for the console config:
```
route:
  canary: traffic_pct: 0.5
  variant: phoenix-27b-x-int8-lite
  fallback: phoenix-27b-x-fp16
  rollout_steps:
    - batch_cap: 1
    - batch_cap: 2
    - batch_cap: 4
  quality_gate: em_delta_threshold: 2.0
```
dmitri: Also add a runtime guard to reject requests that would grow kv-cache beyond a threshold. We had a similar pattern for delta models.
sasha: Good call — I'll add kv-cache trim threshold and a soft-eviction policy for canary. Also will disable aggressive prefetch for int8-lite until we confirm stability.
priya: For the eval regression, can we run logit-diff on token positions where model changed answer? Might point to particular layers/kernels.
kevin: If logit-diff implicates layer-norm/kern-change, consider swapping that layer back to fp16 while keeping others quantized (mixed-precision quant). Minimal cost hit, big quality wins sometimes.
sasha: Plan: I'll run bench tonight, prepare a tiny canary deploy tomorrow 09:00 UTC with batch cap=1 and max_new_tokens=96, attach quality hooks to the eval job and add @eng-oncall for 24h watch. If we still see OOMs we rollback and try soft_mem_reserve tuning.
sasha: tagging folks: @priya @dmitri @ciara @kevin — any objections?
priya: SGTM :thumbsup:
dmitri: No objections. Add an alert rule for OOM rate > 0.1% in 5min.
ciara: Agreed. Also capture some failure traces for the attention kernel to feed to runtime team.
kevin: Nice. Also capture token-latency distributions while you change batch caps.
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: deploy #4576 -> cluster unicorn-prod at 2026-03-22T09:00:00Z (canary traffic 0.5%, batch_cap=1)
sasha: Thanks — I'll post the bench results in this thread tomorrow morning. :coffee:
